items.problem: Bootstrap silently omitted linked authored project items.
items.evidence: lessons.json dev_agent_struggles[0]; session-log.txt turns 2-12; skill-defects.json items[0].
items.root_cause: The bootstrap inventoried the filesystem below -Source rather than the UWP project's effective authored item set.
items.change: Parse UWP project properties and linked Compile/Page/ApplicationDefinition/Content items, copy supported authored files to Link destinations, include them in triage/mapping/meta, and report the linked count.
items.expected_effect: Shared shells, resource dictionaries, code, XAML, and assets enter the normal TODO/mapping workflow instead of being manually reconstructed.
items.falsifiable_check: Against Personalization, bootstrap reports 17 mapped files including 14 linked items and creates App.xaml, MainPage.xaml, Styles\Styles.xaml, and Assets\windows-sdk.png.

items.problem: The documented compile command was invalid, and command ordering did not prevent project-artifact contention.
items.evidence: session-log.txt turns 13 and 23-29; skill-defects.json items[1]; skill-coverage-gaps.json items[0].
items.root_cause: Workflow prose named a nonexistent WinApp CLI command and only implied serialization despite agents batching tool calls.
items.change: Use native synchronous dotnet build commands and explicitly prohibit parallel scaffold/bootstrap/self-check or build/run/validation operations against one project.
items.expected_effect: No unrecognized build command, target-creation race, NuGet restore collision, or locked XAML input.json in a rerun.
items.falsifiable_check: A rerun contains zero 'build was not matched', 'Target not found', restore-collision, or locked-input.json errors.
items.tier_justification: Compilation and orchestration order are agent workflow choices; existing scripts already use dotnet internally, so no template can select and sequence all interactive commands for the agent.

items.problem: Launch diagnostics rejected valid standard dotnet build output.
items.root_cause: Test-AppLaunch.ps1 searched only platform-qualified Debug roots.
items.change: Search bin\Debug after platform-qualified candidates and update diagnostics/documentation accordingly.
items.expected_effect: A normal dotnet build can be smoke-launched without adding Platform solely to satisfy layout discovery.
items.falsifiable_check: Given an app layout at bin\Debug\<tfm>\win-x64, Test-AppLaunch resolves that layout instead of returning 'No build output found under bin\x64\Debug'.
